sources.author: Package authors and contributors

inspected_anchors.finding: Function signature and graph/query contract
stop_on_nonid distinguishes error versus returned nonidentification; expr/steps options expose different results
ID recursion returns an explicit id=false branch for nonidentified results

supported_claims: causal.effect(y,x,z=NULL,G,expr=TRUE,simp=FALSE,steps=FALSE,primes=FALSE,prune=FALSE,stop_on_nonid=TRUE)
The source calls stop when stop_on_nonid is true and otherwise returns empty expression or NULL unless steps requested.
The selected ID implementation returns id=false with witness tree in its steps object.

sources.title: dosearch technical documentation and search source
sources.author: Package authors and contributors

inspected_anchors.finding: Search target, graph classes, multiple source distributions and package output fields
Documentation declares a positive-hour time_limit, identifiable boolean and non-completeness for missing-data problems.
When a positive time limit is enabled, find() returns early; initializer derives identifiable from target_dist size and returns no timeout field.

supported_claims: do-search accepts observational/interventional distributions and selected transport, selection and missingness mechanisms.
A false result is only “not identifiable by do-search” in the package summary; missing-data search is explicitly incomplete.
The pinned C++ path has an early return on time limit before a separate completion state is produced.

sources.title: cfid technical documentation
sources.author: Package authors and contributors

inspected_anchors.finding: The default data level is interventions; observations or both are explicit alternatives.
ID*/IDC* constructs parallel worlds, shares latent variables and reports id/formula/undefined fields.
Counterfactual recursion is distinct from ordinary ID/IDC and can produce probability-zero inconsistent queries.

supported_claims: The function defaults to data=c("interventions","observations","both").
The result can be id=true with an inconsistent conjunction, and undefined=true for a zero conditional denominator.
The source invokes counterfactual graph construction and recursive algorithms.

sources.title: causaloptim technical documentation
sources.author: Package authors and contributors

inspected_anchors.finding: Graph attributes and response-function linear problem are required.
opt_effect returns lower or upper bounds from a symbolic optimization object.
The linear causal problem retains q/p values, constraints, response functions and objective.

supported_claims: The graph must satisfy declared leftside/latent/nvals and edge attributes.
The helper computes either a lower or upper causal-effect bound.
Bounds are restricted to the graph/query/constraint class represented by the constructed linear problem.

sources.title: bpbounds technical documentation
sources.author: Package authors and contributors

inspected_anchors.finding: Binary treatment/outcome/instrument bounds accept trivariate or specified bivariate data.
The R function exposes ACE, intervention-risk, CRR and monotonicity bounds.
Examples use tables/conditional probabilities and do not establish sampling coverage.

supported_claims: The package supports binary outcome, treatment/phenotype and two/three-category instrument.
Outputs include lower and upper ACE and P(Y=1|do(X)) components.
The vignette is an applied package example, not an independent runtime qualification.

sources.title: CausalQueries technical documentation
sources.author: Package authors and contributors

inspected_anchors.finding: Queries can use parameters, priors or posteriors and report means/credible intervals.
Updating uses declared long/compact data and documents missing-at-random assumptions.
The vignette shows posterior query summaries and Stan draws; no package execution is claimed here.

supported_claims: The query result includes mean, sd, cred.low and cred.high and can use counterfactual expressions.
The update contract distinguishes data forms and says missingness is assumed at random in the documented path.
The original vignette records model/posterior semantics and sampling counts as package output examples.
